All Wishes Come True! Review, Cast & Ending Breakdown: Worth Watching?

Key Takeaways for Readers

  • Director Mu Zhengyang reimagines the legendary Eight Immortals as chaotic underdog mortals challenging heaven.
  • Stars Chen Hao and Li Shaozhe lead an energetic voice cast driving slapstick humor and sharp banter.
  • Boasts a strong 8.2 early audience score thanks to dazzling 3D fight sequences and unexpected emotional warmth.
  • Hits theaters on July 10, 2026, delivering an ambitious 143-minute fantasy adventure.
🎯 AUDIENCE & WATCHLIST GUIDE
✓ Who Will Love This:

Fans of high-octane animated spectacles, kung fu comedies, and fresh spins on Eastern mythology will adore every chaotic second.

⚠️ Who Should Pass:

Skip this if you prefer solemn, purist adaptations of classic folklore or get restless during extended two-hour-plus animated films.

How Eight Underdogs Took on the Celestial Realm

All Wishes Come True! flips revered mythology upside down by stripping the legendary Eight Immortals of their typical stoic nobility. Instead, director Mu Zhengyang introduces eight scrappy, working-class misfits who rely on raw hustle and absurd schemes rather than cosmic fate. When an oppressive celestial hierarchy threatens everyday mortal life, this ragtag crew refuses to bend the knee. Using street-level cunning, makeshift gadgets, and relentless audacity, they stumble through mystical realms, clashing with self-important deities who vastly underestimate the power of sheer human stubbornness.

Ending Explained: Do Mortals Truly Defy Heaven?

The climactic showdown pushes the mortal crew to their breaking point as celestial forces unleash apocalyptic judgment. Rather than gaining sudden divine power to overpower the gods, the misfits weaponize the very mortal flaws the heavens look down upon: collective solidarity, unpredictable improvisation, and emotional vulnerability. In a clever narrative twist, they do not dismantle heaven; instead, they force the divine court to recognize their sovereignty. By outwitting the supreme rulers on their own bureaucratic turf, the mortals achieve ascension strictly on human terms, redefining immortality as an enduring legacy of defiance.

Star Voices and Cutting-Edge Visual Craft

Anchoring the comedic friction are voice leads Chen Hao and Li Shaozhe, whose rapid-fire comic timing elevates the banter above standard cartoon antics. Supported by Lidong, Huang Guo, and Dong Tianyi, the voice ensemble brings grounded eccentricity to each distinct character. Behind the curtain, the production team marries traditional ink-wash aesthetics with hyper-kinetic 3D rendering. The combat choreography draws heavily from classic Hong Kong kung fu cinema, resulting in slapstick chases and jaw-dropping aerial duels that make every minute of the sweeping 143-minute duration fly by.

Critical Verdict: Is the 143-Minute Runtime Worth It?

Scoring an impressive 8.2 in early screenings, this rebellious animated romp stands out in an era dominated by cookie-cutter family flicks. While the extended runtime occasionally lingers during secondary subplots, the relentless pacing and lush set pieces maintain momentum. Rated suitable for families and older kids, it offers enough layered social satire to keep adults thoroughly entertained. If you appreciate genre-bending animation that honors cultural folklore while gleefully skewering divine authority, catching this on the biggest theatrical screen possible this July is an absolute no-brainer.
